findings.title: `--json` fix runs still emit prose and can skip JSON entirely
findings.description: In `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:133-207`, `confirm` is computed without checking `opts.json`; in `runRoutedFix` (`packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:229-276`), the no-fixable-findings branch always calls `printCheckOutput(...)` and `console.log(...)`, then returns `null`, so `registerCheckCommand` returns without calling `printJson`. The confirmation branch also prints the dry run and fix plan and calls `askConfirmation`; `packages/cli/src/utils/confirm.ts:7-17` writes the prompt to `process.stdout`. Thus `--json --fix --yes` with no fixable findings produces human text and no JSON, and `--json --fix` without `--yes` can prompt and pollute stdout. Treat `--json` as non-interactive/error early, and always emit a JSON result for no-op paths.

findings.title: CLI and MCP duplicate the routed-fix orchestration
findings.description: `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:133-207` and `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts:259-298` now contain parallel implementations of fix-mode detection, `buildAttributedViews`, invoking-checkout resolution, `scopeViews`, `runCheck`, `runAttributed`, `planRoutedFixes`, and `applyFixPlan`. Only the low-level core helpers are shared, despite comments near `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts:254-259` explicitly aiming to prevent drift between the two consumers. This violates the project’s DRY rule and makes future fixes — for example the JSON guard above or runtime validation of plan inputs — easy to apply to one consumer only. Extract one shared orchestration function for the common plan/apply sequence.

findings.title: Missing runtime validation of `subjectIndex` silently routes fixes to the primary checkout
findings.description: In `packages/core/src/introspection/routedFixes.ts:141-168`, `fixableOf` only checks `f.fixable && f.fixAction`, and `routeView` passes `finding.fixAction!.subjectIndex` directly to `resolveFixOwner`. `packages/core/src/introspection/fixOwnership.ts:34-52` treats any non-null value as an index; if a serialized or mocked result supplies `undefined`, `isInIndexRange` comparisons fail and the function falls through to `findPrimaryView`. That is a silent fallback to the primary checkout — the project convention says to fail explicitly, and the slice design itself calls this out as the dangerous "forgot `subjectIndex`" case. Add a runtime guard that `subjectIndex` is `number | null` and a regression test for an invalid/missing value.

findings.title: New fix tests rely on unconditional mocks with incomplete findings
findings.description: In `packages/mcp-server/tests/workflowTools.test.ts:498-520`, the fix-result tests use `MOCK_CHECK_RESULT` with `fixable: true` but no `fixAction`, while `mockApplyFixes` returns `MOCK_FIX_RESULT` unconditionally. With the real routing path, `planRoutedFixes` (`packages/core/src/introspection/routedFixes.ts:163-177`) filters out findings without `fixAction`, so a real checker would apply zero fixes; the tests pass only because the mock ignores its input. A similar pattern exists in `packages/cli/tests/commands/check.test.ts`. Update fixtures to include valid `fixAction` values with `subjectIndex`, and assert that `applyFixes` is called with the routed finding subset.

findings.title: Public routed-fix API does not constrain fix target paths to the checkout root
findings.description: `planRoutedFixes` and `applyFixPlan` are exported from `packages/core/src/node.ts`, but their inputs are not validated at that boundary. `packages/core/src/introspection/routedFixes.ts:59-60` returns `relative(viewRoot(view), finding.fixAction!.filePath)` without checking that the result stays inside the root; `routeView` (`packages/core/src/introspection/routedFixes.ts:141-151`) then uses that value in `join(viewRoot(owner), ...)`, and single-checkout plans skip readiness checks entirely. `packages/core/src/introspection/ConsistencyChecker.ts#ConsistencyChecker.applyFixes` writes the original `fixAction.filePath`. A crafted or deserialized result with `../...` can therefore inspect or write paths outside the intended checkout. Validate containment at plan time and reject relative paths beginning with `..`.
